transcript: Meeting header: 2026-12-27 14:00 UTC | Duration: 55 minutes | Attendees: Julia Park, Marcus Li (Redwood) — Nina Patel, Carlos Reyes, Tara Singh (Polaris Retail)

Summary: Quick console-focused walkthrough covering usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and token-level cost breakdown. High-level discussion on dedicated vs hosted for a pilot and security questions (SOC2/KMS/VPC). Next steps: send security pack, run perf benchmark with sample traffic, share pilot pricing.
Topics: Console analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, routing policies, dedicated pilots, VPC & KMS, benchmark plan

[00:00] Julia Park: Hey everyone — thanks for joining. quick agenda, we'll show the console usage analytics, drill into per-route dashboards and then look at the cost breakdown for typical retail workloads. Marcus will drive the demo. Nina, Tara, you good with that?
[00:18] Nina Patel: Yep that's perfect. we're especially interested in per-route cost and how that maps to our promo pages and recommendations flows — also curious about data residency and KMS stuff.

[00:34] Marcus Li: Great. jumping into the console — top-left you can see the overall traffic graph, token volumes and latency percentiles. This is live data but for today I've loaded a demo dataset that resembles a retail pattern (promo spikes + steady browse traffic).

[01:05] Marcus Li: Notice the route breakdown on the left — routes map to API endpoints you define. we show per-route tokens, requests, success rate and per-route unit cost. so you can see which route is driving most of your spend.
[01:38] Carlos Reyes: just to confirm, routes are at the API gateway level — so we can split by model and path?

[01:52] Marcus Li: Exactly. you can tag routes to model variants, region and even quantization profile. we also surface per-model token cost and per-request latency so you can compare e.g., gpt-like large vs a quantized 8-bit variant.
[02:20] Tara Singh: How do you calculate token-level cost? are you showing third-party runtime cost or customer-visible unit cost?

[02:32] Julia Park: Good question. the console shows Redwood's unit economics: token count * unit price + infra adjustments for Dedicated. we also show an estimated infra delta so you can see where dedicated pools save money versus hosted at scale.

[03:05] Marcus Li: here's the cost breakdown panel — token-level, model-level and route-level. i've toggled a filter to show only the recommendations route. you can see the spike during the flash sale and the incremental cost by model variant.
[03:45] Nina Patel: there's a note about caching — do you show savings from prefix/KV cache?

[03:52] Marcus Li: Yeah, we display estimated cost reductions from prefix caching and KV cache hits. there's also a suggestions tab under Optimize that recommends which prompts to cache and batching settings to save tokens without hurting latency.
[04:18] Carlos Reyes: For Dedicated pilot, how would pricing and capacity show in the console?

[04:28] Julia Park: The console will surface reserved capacity metrics and you'd get a dedicated cost view. Marcus can show a mock of the Dedicated dashboard — your throughput targets and SLA metrics map directly to the pool and autoscaling settings.

[04:50] Marcus Li: Switching to the dedicated view — here's the pool summary, GPU type, current utilization, queue depth. we also show model variants pinned to that pool and automatic fallback policies (if pool overloaded it can route to hosted with policy).
[05:20] Nina Patel: Is the fallback automatic? our compliance team prefers explicit policies — we need an allowlist.

[05:30] Marcus Li: You can configure routing policies: strict dedicated-only, prioritized dedicated then hosted fallback, or cost-based routing. policies are per-route so you can make your recommendations route dedicated-only while chat assist uses fallback for peak traffic.
[06:02] Tara Singh: About security — does the console show audit logs and per-token access info?

[06:12] Julia Park: Yes, audit logs, request-level traces, and tokenization summaries are in the observability tab. for Private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM and the console can be run in your VPC for the control plane.
[06:35] Carlos Reyes: On the KMS bit, we need envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in AWS KMS. supported?

[06:43] Marcus Li: Yep supported. for Private and Dedicated we can use your KMS; hosted API supports bring-your-own-key for specific enterprise plans. We'll include the SOC2 + KMS integration notes in the security pack.

[07:10] Marcus Li: Back to analytics — you can run ad-hoc queries on historical data, export to CSV, or hook the data into Looker/Databricks via our metrics export. also the per-route trend line helps find regressions after a model rollout.
[07:42] Nina Patel: How are rollouts handled in the console? can you do canary and A/B by route?

[07:51] Marcus Li: Yes, rollout controls are first-class. you can do canary percentages, A/B with different model variants, automatic rollback on quality regressions (we tie to evaluation sets), and route-level metrics to monitor impact on tokens and latency.
[08:25] Tara Singh: This rollback tied to evals — is that based on our test prompts?
[08:31] Marcus Li: Exactly. you upload a prompt set and quality metrics to Redwood Optimize; it flags regressions and can trigger an automatic rollback if thresholds breached.
[08:50] Julia Park: customers often ask about slotting in Redwood with existing infra — Carlos, for your infra team, is there anything specific you want to see?
[09:05] Carlos Reyes: We need network diagrams and egress expectations. also curious about latency numbers from our APAC region to your hosted endpoints vs Dedicated on cloud provider in region.

[09:20] Marcus Li: For latency we keep per-region percentiles. in the console you can view p50/p95/p99 per-region per-model. we can also run a benchmark from your network to the candidate region — that's part of the perf plan.
[09:48] Nina Patel: Another question — can we map cost to business metrics? e.g., cost per conversion on recommendations?
[09:58] Marcus Li: You can annotate routes with business buckets and export cost by bucket. we also support custom tags so finance can attribute spend to campaigns.

[10:20] Julia Park: i'm going to jump to a saved report — this is an example weekly report that shows per-route spend, tokens, and conversions if you feed in the conversion metric. we can automate scheduled reports to slack/email.
[10:44] Tara Singh: Nice. for the pilot we want scheduled weekly reports for the recommendations route and a daily spike alert during promos.
[10:55] Marcus Li: Alerts are configurable in the console — thresholds on latency, error rate, and cost spikes. you can route alerts to pagerduty/slack/email and assign runbooks.
[11:20] Nina Patel: Regarding compliance — can you expose full request logs for audit while still masking PII?

[11:30] Marcus Li: Yes, we offer configurable redaction policies. for sensitive data we recommend client-side tokenization or a pre-processing step; we can also strip or hash fields server-side based on rules.
[11:55] Carlos Reyes: For on-prem or VPC private control plane, is the entire control plane in our VPC or do you keep any meta services?

[12:06] Julia Park: For private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed. there are hybrid options where we host non-sensitive portions, but we can provide a fully air-gapped deployment on request for regulated workloads.
[12:30] Marcus Li: Quick demo note — you might see a few mis-typed labels in the demo console; ignore those, they're artifact of the demo dataset. real console will be cleaned up per tenant branding.
[12:50] Nina Patel: Are there examples you can share of retail customers who reduced unit cost via batching and caching?
[12:58] Marcus Li: Yes — typically customers see 20-40% token cost reduction with prefix cache + workload-aware batching. i'll include anonymized case studies in the follow-up.
[13:18] Julia Park: i'll highlight that in the notes. also we'll include a benchmark spreadsheet template — that'll help you share traffic patterns and we'll run a simulated pilot.
[13:35] Carlos Reyes: On the pilot — duration and commitment? we're thinking 3 months dedicated pool with a usage commit. what's typical?

[13:46] Julia Park: Typical pilot is 1-3 months. for dedicated pilot we do a short-term reserved capacity with a convertible credit model — if you convert to annual commit, pilot credit applies to first invoice. i'll send details in the pricing doc.

[14:05] Marcus Li: i'll call out the metrics we'll measure in the benchmark: p95 latency, tokens per request, concurrency, and cost per 1M tokens. we'll need sample payloads and a traffic replay to run accurate sims.
[14:28] Nina Patel: we can provide a week of traffic and a set of representative prompts. also note data residency — EU-only for a subset of traffic.

[14:40] Julia Park: noted — we'll include region pinned pools for EU traffic in the recommendation. ok shifting to the Optimize tab — this is where we surface ML-driven suggestions: model/quantization combos, batching window suggestions and which prompts to cache.
[15:10] Marcus Li: Example: the recommendation route sees many repeated prefixes. Optimize flags those and suggests KV cache with a TTL of 30 minutes which saved token volume in the demo by ~28%.
[15:34] Tara Singh: Can Optimize do regression detection after model swaps?
[15:40] Marcus Li: Yup — we tie to prompt sets and scoring functions. if quality dips beyond your threshold, it raises an alert and can stop the rollout.
[16:00] Nina Patel: A practical question — what SDKs and webhooks exist for integrating these metrics into our internal dashboards?

[16:08] Marcus Li: We expose a metrics API, webhooks for alerts, and SDKs for telemetry. common pattern is sending per-route tags to a Snowflake or streaming metrics into Datadog via our export connector.
[16:30] Carlos Reyes: Are there quotas or soft-limits for the metrics API?
[16:36] Marcus Li: There's rate limits but we can uplift them for enterprise plans. we'll include the specific numbers in the API docs we send.
[16:55] Julia Park: we're about halfway through — any blockers so far?

[17:02] Nina Patel: main blockers: security + KMS integration confirmation, pilot pricing, and a perf benchmark that matches our real traffic. once we have those, we'll be comfortable starting a pilot.

[17:18] Marcus Li: Great. i'll outline the benchmark steps now: 1) Polaris shares sample payloads & traffic profile, 2) Redwood configures a dedicated test pool in EU and us-east, 3) Run replay for 48-72 hours to measure costs & latency, 4) Analyze and iterate.
[17:44] Tara Singh: timeline?
[17:48] Marcus Li: if we get samples this week, we can kick off within 10 business days. benchmarking run itself takes 2-3 days and analysis another 2-3 days.
[18:05] Carlos Reyes: about data exports for audits — do you store raw request payloads or only traces?
[18:13] Julia Park: by default we store traces and aggregated metrics. raw payload storage is opt-in with retention controls; we can set TTLs and redaction rules per customer.
[18:34] Nina Patel: For SOC2 proof, can you share the cert and the last audit report?
[18:41] Julia Park: yes we'll include SOC2 report in the security pack. also in that pack: network diagrams, KMS flow, redaction examples, and contact for the security review.

[19:00] Marcus Li: jumping back to console features — here's an example per-route drilldown: tokens by prompt type, top prompts, median latency and suggested optimizations. you can export top-n prompts to build caching rules.
[19:28] Tara Singh: That export will help product triage expensive prompts. good.
[19:35] Nina Patel: Any gotchas for model quantization and quality?

[19:40] Marcus Li: Quantization typically yields cost/throughput wins; we show expected quality delta. Optimize recommends quantization only where quality thresholds are met; you'll be able to A/B test in rollout.
[20:05] Carlos Reyes: We're going to need SSO (SAML) and RBAC for teams.
[20:12] Julia Park: Supported — SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. we'll include best-practice role templates for infra/product/ops in the onboarding docs.
[20:35] Marcus Li: Example alert automation: when p95 latency > 800ms on recommendations, mute non-critical routes and increase pool scale automatically, with a slack alert to ops.
[20:58] Nina Patel: That automation sounds useful. we have strict budgets so auto-scaling needs budget guardrails. can you set cost-based limits?

[21:08] Marcus Li: Yes — cost guardrails are part of the autoscale policies. you can set hard caps, soft caps with notifications, and scaling policies that prefer cheaper model variants when nearing budget.
[21:36] Tara Singh: Let's talk handoff — what will we get in the follow-up?
[21:42] Julia Park: We'll send: security pack (SOC2 + KMS diagrams), pilot pricing, benchmark template + instructions, and a short recording of today's demo. Marcus will own the benchmark plan.
[21:58] Marcus Li: I'll also include example config for route tagging, a sample caching rule, and an anonymized case study for retail customers showing token savings.
[22:15] Nina Patel: Perfect. any final technical questions?
[22:20] Carlos Reyes: Not right now, we'll sync internally and send sample data. one ask — can you include an estimate of cost delta between hosted and a small dedicated pool for 1M daily tokens?
[22:35] Julia Park: Yes — i'll include a cost delta worksheet in the pricing doc with a few scenarios. that will help you decide pilot size.
[22:50] Tara Singh: Sounds good. thanks all — this was helpful.

[22:57] Julia Park: Great. quick recap: Polaris to share sample traffic & residency constraints, Redwood to send SOC2/security pack, pricing, and benchmark plan. we'll plan to start perf tests upon sample receipt.
[23:15] Nina Patel: Thanks — we'll aim to send samples by end of week.
[23:22] Julia Park: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and schedule the benchmark kickoff. ending now.
Meeting end: 14:55 UTC
